extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, patent applicants/agents, and KIPO examiners handling representation and powers of attorney under the Korean Patent Act
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for who may represent parties in patent-, utility model-, design- and trademark-related proceedings before the Korean Intellectual Property Office and Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board, including types of representatives, powers of attorney, special authorities, sub-agency, appointment, replacement, and evidentiary requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only registered patent attorneys may act as patent attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a person is a qualified patent attorney, an unregistered patent attorney cannot carry out proceedings as a patent attorney; there should be punishment if that person has conducted business as a patent attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person who is not a patent attorney shall not use the title of patent attorney or similar titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on handling a case previously handled for the opposing party (Article 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent attorney shall not handle a case which he has previously handled as a representative of the other party of the same case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such conduct is a conflict and viewed as deficiencies in granting power of attorney; examiners shall order amendment under Article 46 of the Patent Act and may invalidate proceedings if deficiencies are not addressed. Note and example clarify that prior unrelated representation (e.g., filing/registration of a trademark vs later invalidation action) is not automatically an Article 7 violation (Supreme Court Case No. 81 Hu 51).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: legal representative vs contractual representative
rubrics_metrics.description: A legal representative is empowered by legal provisions (not by principal's intention) to protect persons incapable of conducting lawsuits; representatives appointed by court order or by KIPO appointment are contractual representatives (appointment made by the principal) rather than legal representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority and consequences differ depending on whether representation is legal (by law) or contractual (by principal/appointment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation, change, extinguishment of legal representation follow Civil Act
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle the generation, change and extinguishment of the authority for legal representation shall be made according to the Civil Act; proceedings are interrupted when a legal representative dies or loses authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds for extinguishment include death of principal or legal representative, adjudication of incompetency or bankruptcy, resignation or removal of guardian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope differences between persons with parental authority and guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: A person with parental authority can conduct any patent-related proceedings including trial or retrial without consent of a guardian supervisor; a guardian may conduct proceedings initiated at the request of the other party (e.g., trial/retrial) without guardian supervisor consent but must obtain guardian supervisor consent to perform acts relating to acquisition, forfeit or alteration of rights or to file a petition for trial/retrial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the Civil Act similar restrictions apply; guardian must obtain consent of guardian supervisor for certain major acts (list of six types in Note). Examiners may accept certified copies of resident registration or family relations certificates as evidential documents for parental authorities; guardians must submit evidential documents of consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to declare legal representative in application documents and submit evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a legal representative conducts a patent-related proceeding, he/she shall state such facts in the 'Agent' box in a patent application cover sheet, etc., and submit evidential documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner can confirm the legal representative via the inter-organizational resident registration database, the examiner need not require submission of evidential documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractual representative: creation and extinction of power
rubrics_metrics.description: A contractual representative receives credentials from a principal and the power of representation is generated when a principal grants power of attorney; the power is extinguished when the principal withdraws the empowering authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Act contains special provisions (survival of power) so that power of representation does not lapse on e.g., death or loss of legal capacity of the principal, dissolution by merger, or death of legal representative, to avoid invalidating urgent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special authorities not implied by general power of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: A representative (except a patent administrator of an overseas resident) cannot perform certain acts unless he/she obtains special authority: converting, abandonment or withdrawal of an application (including patent term extension withdrawal), abandonment of a patent right, withdrawal of patent application, withdrawal of request, withdrawal of Domestic Priority under Article 55(1), petition for trial or designation of subagent under Article 132(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrases like 'all matters regarding to the application' in a power of attorney do not include these special authorities unless expressly stated. Special authority must be explicitly described when relating to priority claims or other named special acts; sample power-of-attorney wording is provided in guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special authority required for domestic priority claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The special authority is required to represent a patent application accompanying a domestic Priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show how to word the power of attorney to grant special authority related to priority claim or its withdrawal (reference to Article 55(1) or Utility Model Act Article 11 applied with Article 55(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency requirement and patent administrator rules for overseas residents
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who has a domicile or place of business in the Republic of Korea can carry out a patent-related proceeding without appointing an agent; an overseas resident cannot carry out a patent-related proceeding or sue administrative decisions unless sojourning in Korea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, an overseas resident filing an international patent application may carry out certain tasks (e.g., submitting translation) without an agent until the reference date, but must appoint an agent within two months from the reference date and notify the Commissioner; failure to notify causes the international application to be deemed withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners' procedure when overseas resident conducts proceedings without patent administrator
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an overseas resident carries out a patent-related proceeding without appointing a patent administrator, an examiner shall give the overseas resident an opportunity to explain within the designated period; failure may result in return of documents and deficiency cannot be cured by later appointing a patent administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent administrator ceases to exist (death, revocation, etc.), the examiner shall contact the principal to urge appointment of a new patent administrator; until a new administrator is appointed, documents may be delivered to the principal by registered airmail with warning notes about delivery effect and need to appoint a new administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jointly filed applications: resident and overseas resident rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application is jointly filed by a resident and an overseas resident, a resident may solely carry out patent-related proceedings (except those in Article 11(1)); an overseas resident cannot carry out proceedings alone without appointing a patent administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For proceedings under Article 11(1), a resident must jointly carry out the proceedings with a patent administrator appointed by the overseas resident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent administrator's scope and special authority
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent administrator of an overseas resident can represent the principal in all patent-related proceedings or lawsuits based on the Patent Act within the scope of the power; however, the patent administrator can withdraw an application or a petition only when given special authority for such procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent administrators act within the scope entrusted similar to normal agents; withdrawal acts require explicit special authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements for appointment/change/revocation of representative
rubrics_metrics.description: An appointed representative shall submit a power of attorney and a notification of appointment of a representative to prove appointment; notification of revocation or change must be submitted to revoke or change the appointed representative; procedures specified in Article 5 Enforcement Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appointed or changed while performing a proceeding (e.g., filing an application), a notification with attached power of attorney shall be submitted. If intermediate proceeding performed with an attached power, the representative is treated to hold power only for that intermediate proceeding unless separate notification filed to continue. A copy of a power of attorney can be submitted with source indicated where content unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners' handling of deficiencies in evidential documents for power of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: Where deficiency is found in evidential documents for the power of attorney, an examiner shall order amendment within a designated period; if deficiency not addressed, the examiner shall invalidate the proceeding for the appointment of a representative and proceedings taken by the representative with defective power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If content of submitted documents differs from content in power of attorney, or incorrect principal name or different seal, examiner requests amendment and may invalidate proceedings if not corrected. If amendment and correct power submitted, the power is deemed ratified by the principal; if not ratified, examiner invalidates proceedings conducted by the representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory contents of a power of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney shall include the indication of the case for representation, the names and addresses of the representative and the principal, authorities empowered and the date of preparing the power of attorney, and shall be signed or sealed by the principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When 'all matters regarding …' is used in Matters for Authorization, special authorities under Article 6 are not deemed included unless specified; similarly, wording for change of applicant must clearly indicate subsequent proceedings to be covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority of representative must be proved in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority of a representative (including patent administrator) shall be proved in writing; absent evidential documents, incorrect principal name, or seal mismatch shall be deemed representation without authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner shall request amendment and submission of a correct power; upon correction the power may be ratified; if not ratified, proceedings are invalidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: General power of attorney registration and use
rubrics_metrics.description: The general power of attorney system grants power for all future cases without specifying the case; evidential documents must be attached to a request for registration and submitted to the Commissioner, who grants a registration number which must be stated in documents submitted to KIPO or the IP Trial and Appeal Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registered person may request restriction of reliance on the general power for particular proceedings or withdraw registration; where revocation of a representative is submitted for an application filed by a representative holding general power, it is deemed that a request for restriction of reliance is submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal/resignation from general power of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: A representative holding general power of attorney who intends to resign from particular proceedings or from position of agent with general power must submit a written withdrawal of registration of general power of attorney as defined in Enforcement Rules (Annexed Form No.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural note on form and filing under Article 5(4) Enforcement Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner/President may appoint or replace representatives ex officio
rubrics_metrics.description: Where principal or representative is recognized not to be able to perform administrative proceedings smoothly due to lack of legal capacity, Commissioner of KIPO or President of the IP Trial and Appeal Board can order appointment of a representative or order another representative ex officio; a patent attorney can be ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This authority extends to cases where a patent attorney is designated but lacks capacity (e.g., health, inability to make oral statements); such attorney is deemed incapable of conducting proceedings and another representative may be appointed for administrative convenience and protection of principal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation of proceedings after order for appointment/replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner or the President can invalidate proceedings conducted by the principal or the representative before the KIPO or the Board in the period after the order for appointment or replacement or before appointment/replacement is carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects administration and the principal during the transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-agency: appointment, limits, and evidential proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Sub-agency is authorization by a representative to another person to conduct acts within the representative's scope; the right to appoint a subagent is based on principal approval or legal provisions. A legal representative generally has the authority to appoint a subagent; contractual representatives or patent administrators require special power to appoint subagents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidential documents proving (1) that principal granted authority to appoint a subagent and (2) that the agent appointed the subagent must be submitted (a power of attorney commonly used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for acts of subagent
rubrics_metrics.description: A legal representative is responsible for all acts of his/her subagent regardless of appointment or supervision errors (except unavoidable reasons). A contractual representative is responsible for damages to the principal only when negligent in appointment/supervision; if subagent designated by principal, contractual rep liable only when aware subagent was unfit and failed to notify or revoke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different standards of liability apply depending on legal vs contractual representation and negligence knowledge of unfitness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limits for subagent and prohibition on further delegation
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of authority exercised by a subagent cannot exceed the scope of authority of the representative; in principle, a subagent is not allowed to appoint a further subagent unless the principal expressly granted such power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If representative has special power including appointing subagent, he/she may grant the special power to the subagent as well; otherwise no further delegation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of subagent authority despite certain events
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority of a subagent to conduct patent-related proceedings shall not be extinguished upon death or loss of legal capacity of the principal, extinction of a juristic person due to merger, termination of duty of trust of principal, decease or loss of capacity of legal representative, or modification/extinction of representative authority; unlike Civil Act, Civil Procedure Act and patent provisions keep subagent authority to ensure smooth proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Power of representation of a subagent is not extinguished upon death of a representative for the swift execution of proceedings; extinguishment occurs for causes for lapse under Article 127 of Civil Act or appointment/removal of representative/subagent as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple representatives and independent representation principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there exist many attorneys or two or more representatives, each of them shall represent the principal independently before KIPO or the IP Trial and Appeal Board; agreements to the contrary are ineffective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle of individual representation applies among appointed representatives, principal and representative, representative and subagent, principal and subagent. Example: if multiple representatives each submit a written amendment in response to a notice of grounds for rejection, all amendments shall be deemed legitimately submitted; examiner confirms the specification to be examined and proceeds accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactive effect of ratification for proceedings by unauthorized or incapacitated persons (Article 7(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent-related proceeding conducted by a person who lacks legal capacity, power of legal representation, or necessary authorization shall have effect retroactively to the time when the proceedings were performed if the proceedings are ratified by the principal when he/she has gained legal capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This means proceedings by an incompetent or unauthorized agent take effect retroactively if later ratified by a legitimate principal (e.g., a minor reaching legal age).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint parties and common representative rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Where more than two parties involved jointly conduct a patent-related proceeding, each represents them all except for actions that could disadvantage other parties; matters requiring joint conduct are similar to those needing special power under Article 6. Where common representative(s) are appointed and notified, only the common representative can conduct the proceeding, and evidential documents proving common representation and the power of attorney must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A common representative must have special powers to conduct proceedings under Article 11(1); if a common representative conducts such proceedings without special power, the commissioner shall request amendment and may invalidate the proceeding if deficiencies are not addressed.
